title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals: On-Site Interpreter Days for In-Person Sessions
content:
For an in-person session of Unemployment Insurance Appeals at the Department hearing office, the on-site interpreter days are read from the latest interpreter request on the appeal, that is, the request with the most recent request date.

**Standard.** The on-site interpreter days are the on-site sign-language days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for American Sign Language, the on-site contract-interpreter days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for a language other than American Sign Language and Spanish, and zero days when the latest interpreter request is for Spanish or no interpreter is requested. These days are added to the room block gap, and the set hearing date is moved later by the total before the calendar-day rule is applied.

| Latest interpreter request on the appeal | On-site interpreter days |
|---|---|
| American Sign Language | 5 (on-site sign-language) |
| a language other than American Sign Language and Spanish | 3 (on-site contract interpreter) |
| Spanish | 0 |
| none | 0 |

## Points of judgement

- Earlier interpreter requests on the appeal do not count once a later one is recorded.
- Spanish gives no on-site interpreter days, whether or not an earlier request was for another language.

*Hypothetical cases:* requests for Somali (1 April) then Spanish (6 April) — 0 days; Spanish (1 April) then American Sign Language (6 April) — 5 days; a single request for Hmong — 3 days.
